Frozen live row:
Title: Design a Compliance and Audit Monitoring Solution
Slug: design-a-compliance-and-audit-monitoring-solution
Description: Design a compliance monitoring system that tracks configuration changes, detects security threats, ensures regulatory compliance, and provides centralized audit logging.
Difficulty: Hard
Category: AWS - Security & Compliance
Domain: infra
Estimated time: 60-90 minutes
Requirements (verbatim):
- Track all resource configuration changes
- Audit API calls and user activity
- Detect security threats
- Ensure compliance with standards
- Generate compliance reports
- Remediate non-compliant resources
- Alert on security findings
- Maintain audit logs for 7 years
Constraints (verbatim):
- Comply with PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2
- Detect threats in real-time
- Immutable audit logs
- Automated compliance checks
- Centralized logging across accounts
Hints (verbatim):
- AWS Config for resource tracking
- CloudTrail for API logging
- Security Hub for security posture
- GuardDuty for threat detection
- Config Rules for compliance
- Systems Manager for remediation
Tags: aws, compliance, security, cloudtrail, config, guardduty
Companies: Amazon, Financial Services, Healthcare

The service choices and graph below are a review proposal. The brief supplies no account or resource counts, event rates, detection-latency target, regional policy, or detailed control mapping.

steps.phase: Frame the compliance scope and preserve the supplied brief
steps.title: Confirm which accounts and resources are in scope
steps.content: Centralized logging across accounts is explicit, but the organization structure, account membership, regions, resource types, and exclusions are not. Treat the account estate as a boundary to discover; do not infer that every account or region is enrolled.

decision.question: Which accounts, regions, and resource types must participate in monitoring and centralized audit?
decision.chosen: Inventory the approved scope with the organization and control owners before enabling recorders, trails, or delegated administration.
decision.chosenReason: Coverage and compliance evidence are meaningful only when the monitored boundary is explicit.

alternatives.tradeoff: This would fail to establish the required centralized logging across accounts.

alternatives.option: Assume every account and region is automatically in scope
alternatives.tradeoff: The prompt does not define the organization boundary, exclusions, or regional policy.

steps.phase: Frame the compliance scope and preserve the supplied brief
steps.title: Map named standards to controls without claiming certification
steps.content: PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2 are supplied constraints. Their applicable versions, in-scope systems, control owners, evidence expectations, and assessment boundaries are not. Use an approved control mapping as input to rules and reports; a service configuration or generated report alone does not establish compliance or certification.

decision.question: What approved control set and evidence does each standard require for this environment?
decision.chosen: Ask compliance owners to provide the applicable control mapping and evidence rules before declaring controls satisfied.
decision.chosenReason: The problem names standards but does not specify their scope, versions, or interpretation.

alternatives.option: Treat a vendor security posture score as proof of compliance
alternatives.tradeoff: A posture summary is not a complete control assessment or certification.
An invented mapping can omit applicable controls or report unsupported conclusions.

steps.phase: Frame the compliance scope and preserve the supplied brief
steps.title: Make real-time detection a measurable service objective
steps.content: The prompt says to detect threats in real time but gives no event-to-finding or finding-to-alert deadline. Define which event classes matter, when the clock starts, and what delay is acceptable with the security owner; do not add a numeric SLO here.

decision.question: Which threat events must be detected and alerted on, and how will the owner define acceptable timeliness?
decision.chosen: Keep the event path observable and record the agreed timing objective after discovery.
decision.chosenReason: A qualitative real-time requirement cannot be proven by an invented latency value.

alternatives.option: Claim real-time behavior from selecting a managed detector
alternatives.tradeoff: Service selection does not establish end-to-end detection or notification delay.
No numerical target is present in the live problem row.

steps.phase: Frame the compliance scope and preserve the supplied brief
steps.title: Treat seven-year retention and immutability as separate controls
steps.content: The live row requires audit logs for 7 years and separately requires immutable audit logs. Design the archive to enforce both. Confirm when the retention period begins, which log classes it covers, whether legal holds apply, and which approved Object Lock mode satisfies policy before configuring retention.

decision.question: What retention start point, record classes, legal-hold behavior, and immutable-storage mode are approved?
decision.chosen: Use a protected central archive with retention configured to meet the stated 7-year requirement after the record policy is approved.
decision.chosenReason: The duration is supplied, while the retention semantics and lock policy are not.

alternatives.option: Use ordinary deletable object storage and rely on an operational promise
alternatives.tradeoff: That does not enforce the immutable-log constraint.

alternatives.option: Choose an irreversible retention mode without policy review
alternatives.tradeoff: An incorrect lock policy can prevent required deletion or fail the audit requirement.

steps.phase: Frame the compliance scope and preserve the supplied brief
steps.title: Keep collection, review, and remediation permissions distinct
steps.content: Use separate least-privilege roles for recording and exporting evidence, operating the security services, reading reports, and invoking remediation. Confirm ownership and approval rules for sensitive fields and automated actions. These are policy questions to resolve, not additional compliance controls assumed by this draft.

steps.phase: Record configuration and API evidence across accounts

steps.phase: Record configuration and API evidence across accounts
steps.title: Prove the archive retention and immutability policy
steps.content: Test the configured retention and Object Lock behavior with audit and legal owners. Confirm the retention start point and treatment of exceptions or legal holds; the supplied 7-year duration must be preserved without guessing those semantics.

decision.question: What evidence demonstrates that an audit record remains immutable and available for the required retention period?
decision.chosen: Validate the approved bucket policy, Object Lock configuration, retention behavior, and access controls with representative audit records.
decision.chosenReason: A diagram or storage setting alone does not prove end-to-end retention and immutability.

alternatives.option: Treat versioning by itself as immutable retention
alternatives.tradeoff: Version history does not by itself prevent privileged deletion or establish the required retention policy.

alternatives.option: Apply a retention mode before confirming policy
alternatives.tradeoff: The wrong mode can conflict with required deletion, legal hold, or evidence handling.

steps.phase: Aggregate security findings and route alerts
steps.title: Set an explicit approval and recovery policy
steps.content: The brief requires remediation but does not say which findings may be corrected automatically. Classify actions by impact, define approval and rollback expectations with owners, and make retries safe for the selected runbooks.

decision.question: Which non-compliant resources may be remediated automatically, and which require human approval?
decision.chosen: Require an owner-approved rule-to-runbook mapping and an explicit approval policy before enabling each action.
decision.chosenReason: Remediation can change production resources, and the prompt does not grant blanket authorization for automatic changes.

alternatives.tradeoff: Some findings may require context, create service impact, or represent an intentional exception.

alternatives.option: Leave every non-compliant resource for manual handling
alternatives.tradeoff: This may not satisfy the requested remediation workflow or its operational expectations.

steps.phase: Validate coverage without inventing scale targets
steps.title: Use measured coverage and delivery lag as review signals
steps.content: No account count, event rate, or numeric response target is supplied. Use observed account and resource coverage, rule evaluation health, finding delivery lag, and archive delivery failures to find gaps; agree thresholds with system owners before treating any value as an SLO.

scaleTrigger.metric: In-scope account and resource coverage, plus configuration, finding, and audit-record delivery health
scaleTrigger.action: When coverage is missing or delivery is delayed, identify the affected account and service path, correct enrollment or delivery configuration, and record the evidence gap for report consumers.
scaleTrigger.impact: Operations can identify silent collection gaps without asserting an unsupported traffic or latency target.

steps.phase: Validate coverage without inventing scale targets
steps.title: Make report evidence and its limits visible
steps.content: Agree which control owners, evidence sources, evaluation windows, exceptions, and coverage gaps belong in each report. State the evidence observed and its scope; do not label the system or organization compliant solely because a rule passed or a finding is absent.

decision.question: What evidence and caveats must a reviewer see before using a generated report?
decision.chosen: Show the approved control mapping, evidence source and time, resource scope, exceptions, and known collection gaps alongside results.
decision.chosenReason: A traceable report supports review without turning an incomplete observation into a compliance claim.

alternatives.option: Show only a pass or fail summary
alternatives.tradeoff: Reviewers cannot trace the result to source evidence or identify scope gaps.

alternatives.option: Treat no finding as a passing control
alternatives.tradeoff: Missing telemetry or unsupported controls can also produce no finding.

steps.title: Review the open decisions before implementation
steps.content: The draft now connects configuration tracking, API audit, threat findings, control evidence, reports, approved remediation, alerts, and a protected audit archive. Before implementation, resolve account and regional scope, control mappings, event selection, real-time measurement, immutable-retention semantics, report access, and remediation approval. No traffic volume, numeric SLO, or additional requirement has been inferred.
